newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Afghan Taleban report battle with Shi'ite militia.
newsitem.headline: Afghan Taleban report battle with Shi'ite militia.

text.p: Afghanistan's Taleban militia beat back an attack by an opposition Shi'ite Moslem faction in the Shekhali district of Parwan province on Friday, Taleban-controlled Voice of Shariat radio said.

The radio, monitored in Islamabad, said dozens of fighters loyal to Karim Khalili, leader of the Shi'ite Hezb-i-Wahdat faction, had been killed in the battle. It said 11 Hezb-i-Wahdat men had been captured and eight wounded.
No independent account of the fighting was available.
The Taleban Islamic militia has been trying to advance into Shi'ite-dominated Bamiyan province, northwest of Kabul, as part of its effort to dislodge opposition forces from the north.

Hezb-i-Wahdat is regarded as the weakest link in a northern opposition alliance that also includes General Abdul Rashid Dostum's ethnic Uzbek troops and Tajik fighters loyal to former government commander Ahmad Shah Masood.
The Taleban want to impose their strict interpretation of Islam throughout war-ravaged Afghanistan.
